meta.description: Batch utility program that maintains the Transaction Type reference table by processing a sequential input file to add, update, or delete transaction type codes and their descriptions.
meta.process_description: COBTUPDT reads a sequential input file containing transaction type maintenance instructions and applies each record to the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table. Each input record carries an operation code (A=Add, U=Update, D=Delete) along with a two-character transaction type code and a 50-character description. The program processes all records sequentially until end-of-file, performing the corresponding database operation for each valid instruction. Any invalid operation code, missing record, or database error causes the program to abend with return code 4 and an error message, ensuring data integrity of the reference table.

files.INPFILE: Sequential input file containing transaction type maintenance instructions (add, update, delete) to be applied to the reference table
files.TRANSACTION_TYPE: Database reference table holding the master list of valid transaction type codes and their business descriptions used across the CardDemo system

business_rules: Only three operation types are valid: A (Add), U (Update), D (Delete); any other value except the comment marker (*) causes an immediate abend with return code 4.
Lines prefixed with '*' are treated as comments and are silently ignored, allowing annotated input files.

A transaction type code (TR_TYPE) must already exist in the reference table for Update and Delete operations; if no matching record is found (SQLCODE +100), the program abends rather than silently continuing.
Any negative SQL error code on any database operation (Insert, Update, or Delete) causes an immediate abend, preventing partial or corrupt updates to the reference table.
The program processes records strictly sequentially with no rollback mechanism, meaning records processed before a failure are permanently committed to the database.
The transaction type code is exactly 2 characters and the description is capped at 50 characters, enforcing the data standards of the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table.
This is a reference data maintenance program; changes to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table affect how transactions are classified and reported across the entire CardDemo system.

variables.name: WS-INPUT-VARS
variables.description: Business meaning: Group record structure that holds the parsed fields from an input maintenance instruction before they are validated and applied to the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table. Acts as a working staging area for the incoming operation details.

variables.name: INPUT-TYPE
variables.description: Business meaning: Working copy of the operation code indicating what maintenance action to perform on the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table. Valid values are A (Add a new transaction type), U (Update an existing description), D (Delete a transaction type), or * (comment line to be ignored). Any other value triggers an immediate program failure.

variables.name: INPUT-TR-NUMBER
variables.description: Business meaning: Working copy of the two-character transaction type code (primary key) that identifies which transaction type in the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table is to be added, updated, or deleted. This code is used system-wide in CardDemo to classify and report transactions.

variables.name: INPUT-TR-DESC
variables.description: Business meaning: Working copy of the human-readable business description (up to 50 characters) associated with a transaction type code, such as 'Purchase', 'Cash Advance', or 'Refund'. Used when adding a new transaction type or updating the description of an existing one.

variables.name: FLAGS
variables.description: Business meaning: Group structure holding program control flags that govern the flow of the batch maintenance process.

variables.name: LASTREC
variables.description: Business meaning: End-of-file indicator for the input maintenance file. When set to 'Y', it signals that all transaction type maintenance instructions have been read and processed, causing the main processing loop to terminate and the program to conclude its batch run.

variables.name: WORKING-VARIABLES
variables.description: Business meaning: Group structure holding general-purpose working variables used during the batch maintenance process.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG
variables.description: Business meaning: Error message buffer that captures a plain-language explanation of why a maintenance operation failed (e.g., duplicate transaction type code on Add, missing code on Update/Delete, or SQL error). This message is displayed to operators before the program abends, enabling rapid diagnosis of data or processing issues.

variables.name: WS-MISC-VARS
variables.description: Business meaning: Group structure holding miscellaneous working variables used to capture and evaluate database operation results during the maintenance run.

variables.name: WS-VAR-SQLCODE
variables.description: Business meaning: Captured return code from the most recent database operation (Insert, Update, or Delete) against the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table. A value of zero means success, +100 means the transaction type code was not found (triggering an abend for Update/Delete), and any negative value indicates a database error that immediately halts processing to prevent corrupt or partial updates to the reference table.

variables.name: WS-INF-STATUS
variables.description: Business meaning: Two-character file status code returned by the operating system when the input maintenance file is opened. Used to confirm that the sequential input file containing transaction type maintenance instructions is accessible before processing begins; a non-success status prevents the program from running against a missing or unavailable file.

variables.name: WS-INF-STAT1
variables.description: Business meaning: First character of the input file status code, representing the primary category of the file open result (e.g., '0' for successful, '1' for end-of-file condition, '9' for system-specific error). Together with WS-INF-STAT2, it confirms whether the maintenance input file is ready for processing.

variables.name: WS-INF-STAT2
variables.description: Business meaning: Second character of the input file status code, providing the specific sub-reason for the file open result. Combined with WS-INF-STAT1, it gives operators and developers the precise file system condition code needed to diagnose why the maintenance input file could not be opened, if applicable.

variables.name: WS-INPUT-REC
variables.description: Business meaning: Physical layout of each raw record read from the sequential input maintenance file. Defines how the 53-character input record is structured into its three business components: the operation type, the transaction type code, and the description. This is the direct interface between the input file and the program's processing logic.

variables.name: INPUT-REC-TYPE
variables.description: Business meaning: Operation indicator read directly from the input file record specifying what maintenance action to perform on the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table. Valid values are A (Add a new transaction type), U (Update an existing description), D (Delete a transaction type), or * (comment line to be silently skipped). Any unrecognised value causes an immediate program abend with return code 4.

variables.name: INPUT-REC-NUMBER
variables.description: Business meaning: The two-character transaction type code read directly from the input file record, serving as the unique business identifier (primary key) for the entry in the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table to be added, updated, or deleted. This code is the key used system-wide in CardDemo to classify every financial transaction.

variables.name: INPUT-REC-DESC
variables.description: Business meaning: The business description (up to 50 characters) of the transaction type read directly from the input file record, such as 'Purchase', 'Cash Advance', or 'Refund'. Populated into the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table when adding a new transaction type or replacing the description of an existing one during an Update operation.

paragraphs.name: 0001-OPEN-FILES
paragraphs.description: Opens the transaction type maintenance instruction file so the program can begin reading and processing add, update, and delete operations against the reference table. Confirms the file is accessible before any maintenance activity begins, ensuring the program does not proceed without valid input.

paragraphs.name: 1001-READ-NEXT-RECORDS
paragraphs.description: Orchestrates the end-to-end processing of the transaction type maintenance file by reading and applying each maintenance instruction (Add, Update, or Delete) sequentially until all records have been consumed, then cleanly finalising the batch run.

paragraphs.name: 1002-READ-RECORDS
paragraphs.description: Advances to the next transaction type maintenance instruction in the input file, signalling end-of-file when all instructions have been consumed, and logs each active instruction to the operator console for audit visibility.

paragraphs.name: 1003-TREAT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Routes each transaction type maintenance instruction to the appropriate database operation based on the operation code, ensuring that Add, Update, and Delete requests are correctly applied to the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table, while comment lines are safely skipped and any unrecognised instruction triggers an immediate abend to protect data integrity.

paragraphs.name: 10031-INSERT-DB
paragraphs.description: Registers a new transaction type code and its business description into the CardDemo reference table, making it available system-wide for transaction classification. Confirms successful registration or abends the program if the database rejects the new entry, protecting the integrity of the reference data.

paragraphs.name: 10032-UPDATE-DB
paragraphs.description: Applies an Update instruction to the TRANSACTION_TYPE reference table by replacing the business description of an existing transaction type code. Validates the outcome and abends with an error if the transaction type code does not exist or a database error occurs.

paragraphs.name: 10033-DELETE-DB
paragraphs.description: Removes a transaction type code and its description from the CardDemo reference table, permanently retiring it from the system. Validates the outcome to ensure the deletion was successful, aborting with an error if the code does not exist or a database failure occurs.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND
paragraphs.description: Terminates the program abnormally when a critical processing error has occurred, surfacing the failure reason and signaling to the job scheduler that the batch run ended in error, preventing any further reference table updates.

paragraphs.name: 2001-CLOSE-STOP
paragraphs.description: Finalizes the transaction type maintenance session by releasing the input file after all maintenance instructions have been processed. This ensures the input file is properly closed before the program terminates.
